sections.h2: How quickly can a Midland house change hands?
sections.html:
Quickly, when the price reflects condition. Midland has an energy-driven economy, and investors, landlords and cash buyers all buy there. The usual trade applies: speed and certainty against top price.

Ask every buyer how long a written offer stays open, and compare the offers side by side.

sections.h2: What does the Midland economy mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Midland calls itself the heart of the Permian Basin, and its fact sheet lists Chevron, Diamondback Energy, Midland ISD, Midland Health, the city itself and H-E-B among major employers. ConocoPhillips, ExxonMobil, EOG Resources, Oxy and AST SpaceMobile also have headquarters or regional campuses there.

The city reports a metro population of 193,139 for 2026, growth of 8.1 percent from 2020 to 2026, a median age of 31.5 and an unemployment rate of 3.1 percent. It also states that per capita income ranks second highest in the United States. Its own FAQ notes that apartment rents are rising while occupancy has improved, which is relevant if your buyer is an investor.

  • Midland International Air and Space Port serves American, Delta, Southwest and United.
  • The city runs a Midland Development Corporation that offers business incentives.
  • Midland College and Midland ISD are the main education institutions named by the city.

sections.h2: Which selling routes make sense in Midland?
sections.html:
Most owners pick between a listing, a direct cash sale and a local investor. Choose by the house, not by the headline number.

  • Agent listing. Fits move-in-ready houses; you carry repairs and financing risk.
  • Cash buyer. Handles foundation, roof, plumbing or wiring problems and short-notice relocations.
  • Investor with a short close or leaseback. Gives you time to move out.
  • Keep and rent. Practical only if you can manage repairs and turnover from afar.

Compare the net after fees, repairs and carrying costs on each.

sections.h2: Which Midland permits could trip up a sale?
sections.html:
Midland wants a residential permit for new construction, additions, remodels, repairs and detached accessory buildings, pulled by the owner or a licensed, bonded contractor registered with the city.

Work must begin within 180 days of issue, and a permit lapses if building halts for more than 180 days. Requests go by email to the permit clerk, with 25 percent of the fee due at submission and 75 percent at approval; review usually takes 5 to 7 business days. If earlier work went unpermitted, ask the city how to document it before an inspector raises it. The city building permits page has the process.

Short-term rentals also owe the city a seven percent hotel occupancy tax on the price paid.

sections.h2: What property tax relief applies to Midland homes?
sections.html:
Midland homeowners get school-district homestead relief plus local options. The Midland Central Appraisal District lists the amounts for each taxing unit, which matters to a buyer reading your tax history.

sections.h2: What if a tenant or an unwelcome occupant is in the house?
sections.html:
A tenant goes through eviction; someone who entered without permission may qualify for a quicker route. A tenant gets a written notice of at least three days unless the lease differs, then a justice court case with a hearing 10 to 21 days after filing.

For a person who is not family and was never a tenant, Property Code chapter 24B lets an owner ask the sheriff or constable to remove them with no court case. Conditions include that the person stayed after being told to leave and no suit is pending. A wrongful removal invites a lawsuit, so confirm each condition with the sheriff's office.

  • A writ of possession cannot issue more than 60 days after judgment, though a court may allow 90 for good cause.
  • Cash buyers often take occupied homes, saving you the wait.

sections.h2: What paperwork should I gather in Midland?
sections.html:
A short list avoids surprises at the title company.

  • Deed and mortgage payoff statement.
  • Newest tax bill and any exemption notice from the appraisal district.
  • Permit records for remodels, repairs or outbuildings.
  • Lease and rent roll for an occupied house.
  • Roof, water or foundation reports.

Midland takes permit requests by email, so keep scans of old permits handy. If one is missing, the permit clerk can be reached at 432-685-7390.

sections.h2: What does Midland's own growth plan say about the city?
sections.html:
The city's strategic plan lists six goals: more quality jobs, a safe and secure city, quality of life and place, clear communication, sound fiscal management, and stronger infrastructure. It also points to a Vision Midland story map covering capital projects, parks, downtown redevelopment and economic zones.

For a seller, those projects matter only as context. Street, drainage or downtown work near your address can change how buyers see the block, so ask the city's planning office what is scheduled near you. The city's fact sheet says sales tax collections grew 54.63 percent from fiscal 2015 to 2025, and that high-income households earning $200,000 or more grew 20.4 percent between 2023 and 2024. Those figures describe the local economy, not any one home's value, so rely on written offers and an agent's comparable sales for pricing.

sections.h2: When do Texas tax bills come due?
sections.html:
Bills mail around October 1 and turn delinquent after January 31. On February 1 a six percent penalty and one percent interest apply, and charges keep climbing monthly.

The January 1 owner carries that year's lien. A title company usually prorates the bill and pays it from your proceeds. A value protest is due by mid-May or 30 days after your notice, whichever is later. The Comptroller's calendar lists every step.

sections.h2: How is an inherited Midland house conveyed?
sections.html:
Whoever signs the deed must prove authority. Depending on the facts, that proof is an administrator's deed, a muniment of title order, a recorded affidavit of death with a transfer on death deed, or finally an affidavit of heirship.

An estate can use a small-estate affidavit if everything beyond the homestead totals $75,000 or less and all heirs agree. See the State Law Library guide.

sections.h2: What should I ask a cash buyer here?
sections.html: Find out who the buyer is, whether the price covers the whole house as is, and who holds earnest money. Ask how many days to close and what happens if a lien surfaces. Read the contract before committing, and let the title company prepare the closing statement.

sections.h2: Why does Midland's population profile matter to sellers?
sections.html: The city reports a median age of 31.5 and a civilian labor force of 106,000. A younger workforce tends to include renters and first-time buyers, so an investor or a buyer using financing may both compete for your house. New-graduate unemployment is listed at 0.4 percent, and median income for college graduates at $64,918. Use these figures as background, then rely on written offers for pricing.

faqs.q: Is selling as-is allowed in Midland?
faqs.a: Cash buyers regularly purchase houses with foundation, roof or plumbing problems. The offer will reflect the repair cost.
Repairs, remodels, additions and detached accessory buildings. An owner or registered bonded contractor applies, and a permit lapses if work does not begin within 180 days.

faqs.q: What homestead relief does a Midland buyer get?
faqs.a: Midland ISD gives $140,000 plus a 10 percent local option, per the appraisal district's table. A purchaser may claim it right away if you never did.

faqs.q: Who settles the tax bill when the sale closes?
faqs.a: The title company, normally, with your share taken from proceeds. The lien attaches January 1, so read the split on the closing statement.

faqs.q: What paperwork proves I can sell an inherited house?
faqs.a: Court or recorded documents showing authority: a muniment of title, administration, a transfer on death deed, or an affidavit of heirship.
